meta.title: Who wrote "I'm a Believer"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: The Monkees' biggest hit — but they didn't write it. "I'm a Believer" was written by Neil Diamond, who later recorded his own version. Who wrote it, and whose version everyone knows.
meta.ogDescription: Not a Monkees original composition. Neil Diamond wrote it in 1966 and recorded it himself the next year — but the Monkees' version is the one that went to No. 1.

writing.label: Written by Neil Diamond — recorded by The Monkees
writing.sourceLine: The Monkees’ biggest hit and one of the best-selling singles of the 1960s — but the band didn’t write it. ‘I’m a Believer’ was written by Neil Diamond, then near the start of his own career, who recorded his own version the following year.

docMeta.dd: US No. 1 (7 weeks), UK No. 1 (4 weeks)

writing.definitiveVersion: The Monkees’ 1966 single — the last US No. 1 of 1966 and the biggest-selling single of 1967.
trail: The song is credited to Neil Diamond on the Monkees’ release and throughout its publishing history; it was produced by Jeff Barry.
Diamond wrote it in 1966 and recorded his own version for his 1967 album Just for You; that version was a minor chart hit when released as a single in 1971.

The Monkees were assembled for a television show and, early on, largely recorded material written by outside songwriters — which is why the writing credit surprises people who take the hit for a band original.

context.heading: The song that made Neil Diamond a hitmaker
lead: ‘I’m a Believer’ is one of the clearest cases of a song the public files under the performer while the writer sits just out of frame. Neil Diamond wrote it early enough that he was better known, at the time, as a songwriter for others than as a star in his own right.

That flipped soon after: the Monkees’ No. 1 helped establish Diamond as a commercial songwriter, and his own performing career followed. The song belongs to both of them — the Monkees’ record, Diamond’s pen.
context.pull: The Monkees' biggest hit was Neil Diamond's early calling card.

authors.name: Neil Diamond
authors.bio: One of the best-selling recording artists of all time, Diamond began as a Brill Building-era songwriter. ‘I’m a Believer’, written for the Monkees, was among the hits that established him before his own performing career took off.

authors.name: The Monkees
authors.bio: Assembled for a television series, the Monkees had their biggest hit with ‘I’m a Believer’ — written for them by Neil Diamond and sung by Micky Dolenz.

schema.faqAnswer: "I'm a Believer" was written by Neil Diamond. It was recorded by The Monkees, whose 1966 version went to No. 1 in the US and UK; Neil Diamond released his own recording of it in 1967.
